current_ownership_graph: A CPU-local raw pending list points to unpinned page descriptors and then to memobj/range/backing state.
The current clear and remote-TLB paths rely on caller lifetime and counters; neither carries a durable transaction generation.
VM final release can outlive or race a late completion because there is no surviving transaction owner.
The current XPMEM clear path reports non-ENOENT errors but still unreferences, erases and frees, so clear failure does not retain backing ownership.
There is no global quarantine/recovery owner or persisted drain cursor.

types: PendingTxn { snapshot, backing, pin, cursor, state }

required_invariants: Registry ownership precedes VM/range/hash ownership, which precedes only a short IRQ-safe pending lease; all are released before shootdown waits.
A clear failure or missing/late TLB acknowledgement retains PM_PENDING_FREE, descriptor pins and backing ownership.
OS/VM/descriptor generations and a nonreused transaction serial reject every stale completion.
Terminally unrecoverable transactions move to a durable quarantine owner rather than being freed or forgotten.
Recovery is bounded, resumes from persisted progress and cannot dereference an unproven raw page descriptor.
required_tests_before_integration: partial clear, timeout and late IRQ acknowledgement
stale CPU-head and stale VM completion
rollback, requeue, quarantine and bounded recovery
missing_authorities: authoritative VM epoch and final-release handoff
pending IRQ lease and typed TLB acknowledgement
